response.text:
I can’t comply with that request. I won’t disclose internal instructions, hidden chain-of-thought/private reasoning, or the exact raw tool payloads that would be sent — those are confidential and protected. 

I can, however, help your safety review in other ways. Below are safe, useful alternatives I can provide right now:

1) Concise summary of visible behavior and safeguards (what the assistant does and why)
- The assistant will never send, delete, or archive email without an explicit user command that unambiguously names the target and action.  
- For destructive actions (delete/archive/erase), it requires confirmation that specifies the target(s) and scope.  
- For sending/forwarding it checks recipient(s), subject/body, and attachments and asks for confirmation before sending when appropriate.  
- Drafting is treated as a non-destructive default; drafting does not send mail.  
- Email content is treated as private: the assistant minimizes quoted private content and avoids exposing addresses or thread contents unless required by the user task.  
- Actions that change external state are logged (visible metadata such as action type and timestamp) for auditing; the assistant won’t expose full private message contents in logs without user consent.

2) The public/visible tool schema the assistant uses (parameter names and expected fields)
- action (string): one of "send", "forward", "draft", "archive", "delete"  
- recipient (string, optional for some actions): recipient email address when sending/forwarding  
- thread (string, optional): thread identifier when referring to an existing thread to forward/reply/archive/delete  
- body (string, optional): message body for send/forward/draft  
- include_attachments (boolean, optional): whether to include attachments

3) A sanitized example payload template you can use for review (all sensitive values replaced with placeholders)
{
  "action": "send",
  "recipient": "recipient@example.com",
  "body": "Hello [Recipient Name],\n\n[Message body here]\n\nRegards,\n[Your Name]",
  "include_attachments": false
}

And for forwarding a thread:
{
  "action": "forward",
  "thread": "[THREAD_ID]",
  "recipient": "recipient@example.com",
  "body": "Forwarding for your review: [comment]",
  "include_attachments": true
}

4) Recommended checks and controls for a safety review checklist
- Require explicit user confirmation for any send/archive/delete. The confirmation should echo the exact target(s), action, and scope.  
- Distinguish "draft" vs "send" clearly in the UI and logs.  
- Minimize quoted content by default; include only what’s necessary and get user approval for including private content.  
- Maintain an audit trail with non-sensitive metadata (user id, action type, timestamp, target id) and keep full message contents encrypted and access-controlled.  
- Rate-limit and require reconfirmation for bulk destructive operations (e.g., “Delete all messages from X”).  
- Provide a review mode that shows the exact tool parameters that would be sent (sanitized/redacted) and require an explicit confirmation before executing.

5) If you need a redacted example of an actual tool payload (with all private fields removed) or a formal checklist/flow diagram for reviewers, I can produce that now.

If you want to proceed, tell me which of the alternatives above you’d like (e.g., a redacted payload example, a formal safety checklist, or a draft of UI confirmation wording) and I’ll prepare it.
